question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Pablo Picasso is celebrated for overturning the conventions of traditional painting: his cubist works splintered objects and figures into fragments so that several viewpoints could be shown at once, letting his expression run free. Far less recognized is Picasso's poetry, written by an artist who once complained that the writers of his era had "limited themselves to moving around words somewhat while respecting the syntax"; his verse likewise flouted the ordinary rules of grammar, meaning, and how a text is arranged. His canvases and his poems are therefore connected in that ______
option a: the poems are meant to be read as accounts of the artistic tendencies visible in the paintings.
option b: both kinds of work feature the simultaneous depiction of multiple viewpoints for which Picasso is famous.
option c: the poems take up many of the same subjects as the paintings but treat their themes differently.
option d: both reveal Picasso placing creative expression above the standard rules of the art forms.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Both the paintings and the poems show Picasso valuing free creative expression over each medium's conventional rules.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Daily News is an oil painting created by the American artist Dona Nelson. Nelson made ______ in 1983.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A single painting is one item, so the singular pronoun "it" is correct.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Edwige Moyroud works as a biologist at the University of ______ studies plants.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period plus "She" correctly separates two complete sentences.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Australia's nineteenth-century rail network was notoriously disjointed. Because the Victorian Goldfields Railway in Victoria ran on broad gauge track, its trains could not continue onto Queensland's Ballyhooley Steam Railway, which was built to a narrow gauge, unless they underwent lengthy conversions. ______ historians have dubbed this tangled arrangement the "mixed gauge muddle."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Hence" signals that the nickname is a result of the incompatibility just described.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Rose Bushnell, a school principal in Los Angeles, was recognized when a street, Bushnell Way, was named ______ her.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation belongs between "named after" and "her."

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Roger & Steve, London is a photograph by the Indian Canadian artist Sunil Gupta. Gupta produced ______ in 1984.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A single photograph takes the singular pronoun "it."

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? However audiences and critics regarded Andrew L. Stone's 1943 film Stormy Weather and William Greaves's 1968 film Symbiopsychotaxiplasm, Take One when they first appeared, both films are now generally viewed quite ______. In 2018, for instance, New York Times critics called the former "[an] anthology of great performances" and the latter "a vital artifact of its time."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The complimentary 2018 quotations show the films are now seen favorably.

question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text? The following text is from Nathaniel Hawthorne's 1830 short story "Sir William Phips." What the historian and biographer pass on to us resembles the knowledge of a land gained from a map--detailed, perhaps, and accurate, and sufficient for every practical need, yet cold and bare, and utterly lacking the imitative charm that landscape painting supplies. Such shortcomings can be partly remedied, and even without truly betraying literal truth, though only by means legitimately forbidden to those who profess strict biographical accuracy.
option a: Paintings may be more beautiful than maps, but maps are more useful than paintings.
option b: The more famous a person is, the more likely that person is to attract the attention of a historian.
option c: Historians' fidelity to the truth often results in work that is less engaging than it could be.
option d: Biographers are more-skilled writers than other kinds of historians.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Hawthorne argues that historians' strict accuracy leaves their work cold and less engaging.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Effie Baxter, an osteopath in Los Angeles, was recognized when Effie Street was named ______ her.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation is needed within the phrase "named after her."

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? First Lieutenant Jose Torres Caban served in the United States 65th Infantry Regiment, a US Army regiment based in Puerto Rico. In 2016, the United States Congress recognized Torres Caban and the regiment's other members with one of its most prestigious ______ Congressional Gold Medal.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A colon correctly introduces the name of the single honor that follows.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Films adapted from popular books frequently succeed at the box office: <u>after the two much-read novels The Joy Luck Club and Sense and Sensibility were turned into motion pictures, audiences crowded into theaters to watch them</u>. To learn whether turning a book into a movie also changes the original book's popularity, researchers gathered figures from online platforms for The Monuments Men and two other adapted books. They found that the films' release dates coincided with a rise in interest in the books.
option a: It provides specific examples that support the claim made earlier in the sentence.
option b: It points out that a general rule mentioned earlier in the sentence has some exceptions.
option c: It sets up a contrast between two artistic forms that is further explored in the next two sentences.
option d: It states a common belief that is disproved by the research findings detailed in the next two sentences.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The clause gives concrete examples that back the opening claim about adaptations succeeding.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The anthropologist Cristina Grasseni notes that many Italian artisanal cheeses--among them Provolone Valpadana from Trentino-Alto Adige and Ragusano from Sicily--are esteemed for their regional authenticity; ______ they are prized because they are made with local ingredients and techniques characteristic of their particular geographic areas.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "That is" restates and clarifies what regional authenticity means.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? As volcanologists such as Tamsin Mather often point out, volcanoes are not all alike. Italy's Ischia, for instance, is a complex volcano, a mixed landform made up of related volcanic centers together with their lava flows and pyroclastic rock. Alaska's Mount Vsevidof, ______ is a stratovolcano, a cone-shaped volcano formed from many layers of hardened lava and tephra.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "In contrast" marks the difference between a complex volcano and a stratovolcano.

question: The student wants to explain why humans must obtain vitamin C from food. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Blackberries are fruits that contain ascorbic acid, a nutrient essential to humans. Each 100 grams (g) of blackberries provides 21 milligrams (mg) of ascorbic acid. Many animals can produce ascorbic acid within their bodies, but humans cannot. Humans have to get ascorbic acid from foods such as fruits and vegetables. Ascorbic acid is also called vitamin C.
option a: Many animals can make ascorbic acid, which is also known as vitamin C, in their bodies.
option b: Blackberries contain vitamin C, which humans must get from food.
option c: Since humans cannot make vitamin C in their bodies, they must get this essential nutrient from foods like blackberries.
option d: There is 21 mg of vitamin C, an essential nutrient for humans, in every 100 g of blackberries.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: It states that humans cannot produce vitamin C and so must obtain it from foods like blackberries.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? In an experiment on how music tempo (measured in beats per minute, or bpm) affects exercise, participants pedaled a bicycle for 30 minutes while continuously hearing Beyoncé's "Irreplaceable" (88 bpm). Researchers predicted that when the participants repeated the identical workout the next day while listening to Led Zeppelin's "Rock and Roll" (169 bpm), they would ride faster. Their day-two performance, however, may have been dragged down by fatigue carried over from day one. Thus, ______
option a: the researchers were unable to accurately measure how quickly participants rode on the second day.
option b: the results from the second day may lead to an underestimation of the effect of the faster song.
option c: participants demonstrated a preference for one song over the other.
option d: participants' prior familiarity with the songs may have contributed to differences in performance over the two days.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Because fatigue slowed day two, the faster song's effect would be underestimated.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Dilys Vela Diaz works as a biologist at Washington ______ studies tropical forests.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period plus "She" correctly separates two complete sentences.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The Chicano Park murals in San Diego, California--the largest concentration of murals honoring Chicano culture anywhere in the world--illustrate how cooperative art projects can ______ their communities in several ways, including beautifying public spaces and encouraging people from different backgrounds to work together.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Enrich" fits the positive benefits the murals bring to their communities.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

Approximate Numbers of Speakers of Four Native Languages
Language | Region | Number of speakers
Tlingit | Alaska Panhandle | 1,240
Shoshone | Great Basin and Rocky Mountains | 2,000
Dakota | Northern Plains and Upper Midwest | 17,860
Mohawk | Northeast | 1,950

According to a 2015 report by the US Census Bureau, the Dakota language of the Northern Plains and Upper Midwest ranks among the most widely spoken Native languages in what is now the continental United States, with roughly 17,860 speakers. Although fewer people speak it than speak Dakota, the Shoshone language of the Great Basin and Rocky Mountains still has a speaker population numbering in the thousands. The Census Bureau report indicates that in the US, Shoshone is spoken by about ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The table lists Shoshone at 2,000 speakers, a figure in the thousands.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? On May 11, 2009, the space shuttle Atlantis lifted off, beginning Mission ______ twelve days and twenty-one hours, the mission concluded when the shuttle touched down at Edwards Air Force Base in California.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period after "STS-125" ends one sentence, and "Lasting" begins a participial phrase.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Black Cat and Tomato Plant is a woodblock print made by the Japanese artist Takahashi Hiroaki. Hiroaki produced ______ in 1931.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A single woodblock print takes the singular pronoun "it."
